messages:
Alice Nguyen: quick q — updating region availability doc. want to add explicit example for customers switching from global -> regional endpoints (Seoul + Frankfurt). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/427
Bob Reed: add a short Ruby snippet too, we only have Node/Python in other PRs
Charlie Park: I'll audit the 'data residency' sentence. We should say: "For hosted regional accounts, data processing and storage occur inside the selected region's legal boundary." avoids 'retain'
Alice Nguyen: added curl + Node + Python + Ruby examples in the PR. Node snippet:
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, region: 'ap-northeast-2' });
await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-7b', input: 'Summarize: release notes' });
```
Bob Reed: Ruby example looks good:
```ruby
client = Redwood::Client.new(api_key: ENV['RW_KEY'], region: 'eu-central-1')
resp = client.generate(model: 'redwood-7b', input: 'Hello')
```
Dana (docs-ci): link-check: internal links ok, external provider map flagged. recommend swapping to internal region matrix asset: /assets/region-matrix.png
legal-bot: Reminder: include DPA link and contact legal@redwood.ai for custom residency agreements. Also avoid absolute claims about 'data never leaves X' unless we have contractual promise.
Charlie Park: updated wording to: "Hosted regional endpoints process and store data within the selected region for standard accounts; bespoke residency commitments require contract." added note about cache locality.
Alice Nguyen: Added migration section showing base URL change:
```bash
# global -> eu
curl -X POST https://eu.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b","input":"hi"}'
```
Bob Reed: pls add a one-liner about rate limits and quotas being per-region and potential warm-up time for caches when migrating
Alice Nguyen: done. will merge after one final quick pass from product writing. thanks! :tada:
